title: "Stress Pipeline Debug — PSS-10 Correlation Validation"
format: html

## What This Code Does

This demo runs a simulation and tracks detailed per-agent data at each step: resilience, affect, stress, PSS-10, coping outcomes, challenge/hindrance values, and social influence. It computes step-by-step correlation matrices to validate that expected theoretical relationships — especially the negative correlation between resilience/affect and PSS-10 — hold throughout the simulation lifecycle.

## Setup

```{python}
#| label: setup
import os
import sys
import pathlib
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

demos_dir = pathlib.Path(os.getcwd())
project_root = demos_dir.parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(project_root))

from src.python.model import StressModel
```

## Simulation and Data Collection

```{python}
#| label: simulate
n_agents, n_steps, seed = 20, 30, 42
model = StressModel(N=n_agents, max_days=n_steps, seed=seed)

records = []
for step in range(n_steps):
    model.step()
    for i, agent in enumerate(model.agents):
        records.append({
            "step": step, "agent": i,
            "resilience": agent.resilience,
            "affect": agent.affect,
            "current_stress": getattr(agent, "current_stress", 0),
            "pss10": agent.pss10,
        })

df = pd.DataFrame(records)
print(f"Collected {len(df)} agent-step records ({n_steps} steps × {n_agents} agents)")
```

## Correlation Over Time

```{python}
#| label: corr_time
# Compute correlation at each step
step_corrs = df.groupby("step").apply(
    lambda g: g[["resilience", "affect", "current_stress", "pss10"]].corr().iloc[0, 3],
    include_groups=False
).reset_index()
step_corrs.columns = ["step", "resilience_pss10_corr"]
print("Resilience-PSS10 correlation by step:")
print(step_corrs.to_string(index=False))
```

## Overall Correlation Matrix

```{python}
#| label: corr_overall
vars_ = ["resilience", "affect", "current_stress", "pss10"]
corr_matrix = df[vars_].corr()
print(corr_matrix.round(4))
```

## Correlation Trends

```{python}
#| label: plot
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 4))
plt.plot(step_corrs["step"], step_corrs["resilience_pss10_corr"], marker=".", color="#3498db")
plt.axhline(y=0, color="gray", linestyle="--", alpha=0.5)
plt.xlabel("Step"); plt.ylabel("Resilience-PSS10 Correlation")
plt.title("Correlation Trend Over Simulation Steps")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Why This Matters for the Simulation

Debugging the stress pipeline is critical for ensuring model validity. The expected negative correlation between resilience and PSS-10 reflects the theoretical understanding that higher resilience buffers against perceived stress. If this correlation breaks down at any point in the pipeline, it indicates a bug or conceptual flaw in the stress processing mechanics. This demo provides the diagnostic tools needed to pinpoint such breakdowns.
